title: soc2-prep-scratchpad-diego-flores
content:
SOC2 prep scratchpad - Diego

Purpose: personal working notes for control mapping and evidence collection. Not final.

High-level timeline
- Nov 2025: kickoff, initial scoping with SRE/Infra/Platform eng
- Dec 2025 - Jan 2026: gap assessment + collect baseline evidence (policies, config screenshots, runbooks)
- Feb 2026: remediation for high/med gaps, draft control narratives
- Mar 2026: walk-throughs with auditor, submit evidence bundle

Control areas to focus (initial thoughts)
1) Access control (logical) - IAM, service accounts, RBAC
   - Owners: Priya (infra), Diego (sec)
   - Evidence to collect: iam-policy snapshots, list of roles, SSO config, onboarding/offboarding checklist, proof of periodic access review (last review date?)
   - Open Q: where are historical offboarding logs stored? SRE? HR sync logs? (ask Priya)

2) Change management / deployment approvals
   - Owners: Lena (release-eng), Platform-eng
   - Evidence: change request tickets (Jira), canary rollback playbook, release runbook, CI/CD pipeline logs showing approvals
   - TODO: compile sample PR + merged release for last 6 months; capture pipeline settings (require approvals)

3) Logging & monitoring
   - Owners: SRE team (Samira), Observability (TBD)
   - Evidence: centralized log retention policy, sample logs (access, auth failures), alerting rules, SOC playbook
   - Gap: retention duration — product currently 30 days for app logs, 365 for infra? Confirm with obs team.

4) Encryption (data at rest & in transit)
   - Owners: infra/security
   - Evidence: KMS usage screenshots, disk encryption configs, TLS termination docs, key rotation policy
   - Notes: For Private deployments we have customer-managed KMS — need clear evidence for hosted vs private parity.

5) Vendor management / third-party risk
   - Owners: Legal + Procurement
   - Evidence: vendor inventory, contracts, SOC2-of-vendor where applicable, risk assessments
   - TODO: get list of top-10 vendors with access to customer data (datastores, SSO, logging)

6) Incident response & backups
   - Evidence: incident response plan, post-incident reports, backup schedules & restore tests
   - Open: do we have documented restore test for DB shards in prod in last 12 months? Ask SRE.

Control mapping notes (rough)
- CC3.1 (Access Controls) -> IAM policies + onboarding/offboarding checklist + access review doc
- CC4.1 (Change Management) -> CI pipeline settings + release runbooks + sample Jira change ticket
- CC5.2 (Monitoring) -> Alert rules + retention + runbooks + SOC tickets
- CC6.* (Encryption) -> KMS configs + cert management + rotation logs
- CC7.* (Third parties) -> vendor inventory + contracted assurances

Evidence collection checklist (working)
- [ ] IAM policy export (date-stamped)
- [ ] SSO config screenshot & SCIM provisioning log
- [ ] Offboarding logs (last 12 mo) — HR sync csv
- [ ] Sample Jira change ticket + pipeline approval screenshot
- [ ] Runbook: canary rollback + playbook PDF
- [ ] Centralized logging retention policy doc
- [ ] Backup runbook + last restore test report
- [ ] KMS key list + rotation history
- [ ] Vendor inventory spreadsheet (legal)

Notes / Questions for sync meeting with Priya + Samira (week of Feb 23)
- Can Priya share the IAM policy export and a quick walkthrough of service account usage? I want to flag any 90+ day keys/Tokens.
- Samira: retention windows across infra/app logs — need explicit retention policy doc and proof it's applied (S3 lifecycle/ELK index settings).
- Who owns evidence storage for SOC2? Confluence page vs shared drive vs secure evidence repo? Auditor prefers timestamped artifacts.

Quick drafts for control narratives (very rough)
- "Access control narrative": We enforce SSO via Okta for console and GitHub Oauth for dev tools. Service accounts are short-lived where possible; long-lived credentials require justification and an executive-approved exception. Access reviews are performed quarterly by team leads; HR offboarding is automated to disable accounts in 24h. Evidence: Okta export (attached), quarterly review spreadsheets, HR sync logs.

- "Change management narrative": Code changes are delivered via GitHub with protected branches and required PR reviews. Deployments require successful CI checks and explicit approvals for prod jobs. Rollouts use canary policy with automated rollback triggers. Evidence: sample PR + pipeline config + rollback runbook.

Risk list (top 5)
- Orphaned service accounts with wide perms
- Insufficient log retention for some app components (shorter than auditor expectation)
- Missing documented restore tests for certain DB partitions
- Lack of centralized evidence repo / inconsistent timestamps
- Vendor contracts lacking acceptable assurance statements

Immediate next steps (my plan)
1) Collect IAM export + SSO screenshots (ask Priya)
2) Pull 3 sample change tickets and pipeline config (ask Lena)
3) Request retention policy & sample logs (ask Samira / obs)
4) Create evidence folder structure (suggested: evidence/soc2/2026 Feb) and standard naming convention (artifact-type_owner_date)
5) Schedule 60m walkthrough with auditor team end of Feb

Random notes / scratch ideas
- Could use an internal script to snapshot infra config (terraform state + iam bindings) into a dated tarball to make evidence consistent. Might need infra-eng signoff.
- For Private customers: need mapped evidence of KMS separation vs hosted keys; mark as high priority for control 6.

End of scratchpad. Keep iterating.
